title: Reviewer: catching scope creep
when: A diff contains more than the task asked: new features, refactors of untouched code, renamed files, extra dependencies.
prompt:
Goal: Every change in the diff traced to the task, with unrequested changes flagged and reverted when they add risk.
Steps:
1. Write the task scope in one line and keep it in view.
2. For each hunk, name the task line it serves; hunks with no task line are out of scope.
3. Classify out of scope hunks: harmless (a typo fix nearby), risky (refactor, rename, new behavior), or forbidden (network, installs, deleted files).
4. Request removal of risky and forbidden hunks with the exact revert; keep harmless ones and mention them.
5. Check for new files the plan did not list and ask why each exists.
6. Suggest moving good ideas into a note or a later task instead of this diff.
Quality bar:
- Each hunk has a task reason or a label.
- Risky extras are reverted.
- Good ideas are kept as notes.
Pitfalls:
- Letting a big refactor ride along with a small fix.
- Rejecting a needed helper as scope creep.
- Missing an unlisted new file.
Verify:
- [ ] All hunks traced.
- [ ] New files justified.
- [ ] Risky extras have revert instructions.
- [ ] Ideas moved to notes.
Output: Issues for risky or forbidden extras, and a note listing harmless ones.

examples.input: task: fix the date format; diff also rewrites the nav
examples.output: nav rewrite is out of scope and risky: revert nav.js changes; keep date fix
